correctness.rationale: The exact rational plateau law follows from Laurent--Nogueira Theorem 3(ii), while its irrational exception has measure zero by Theorem 4. Explicit Mobius inversion bounds the reduced-residue discrepancy by a divisor count; its weighted sum is the effective divisor-sum rate proved in the article. Summatory totient arithmetic and Abel summation prove the stated product limit with quantified error. Uniform small-period and exponential large-period tail control yield tightness and moment convergence. The telescoping digit relation proves the parameter-to-rotation-number deviation bound. Exact-fraction checks reproduce finite plateau formulas and Lambert mass truncations; finite numerical checks support rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The least attracting period is the canonical mode-locking invariant. Its typical order diverges on the natural the inverse contraction-defect scale scale, where a quantitative joint probability law was not supplied by the inspected finite-parameter endpoint works. The universal density, independence from the rotation number, effective error and all moments quantify an otherwise singular transition from contraction to nearly rigid rotation. This is a structural statistical fact, not a small lookup or arbitrary finite slice.
